title: Ethanoic acid content of vinegar
stem: A 25.00 cm³ sample of vinegar was diluted to 250.0 cm³ with distilled water in a volumetric flask. A 25.00 cm³ portion of the diluted vinegar was titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ sodium hydroxide solution. The mean of the concordant titres was 21.60 cm³. Assume ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH (M = 60.06 g mol⁻¹), is the only acid present.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the balanced equation, including state symbols, for the reaction of ethanoic acid with sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the concentration, in mol dm⁻³, of ethanoic acid in the diluted vinegar.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the concentration of ethanoic acid in the original vinegar in g dm⁻³.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A 0.0864 mol dm⁻³ solution of hydrochloric acid has a pH of 1.06. Explain why the diluted vinegar has a higher pH, even though it has the same concentration of acid.
markscheme: ethanoic acid is a weak acid / only partially dissociates / CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺
HCl dissociates completely, so [H⁺] in vinegar is lower and its pH is higher

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: State why the same volume of sodium hydroxide would be needed to neutralize 25.00 cm³ of 0.0864 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid.
markscheme: both acids are monoprotic and contain the same amount (mol) of acid / as NaOH removes H⁺ the weak acid continues to dissociate until all reacts

title: A nickel–silver voltaic cell
stem:
A voltaic cell is built from a nickel electrode in 1.00 mol dm⁻³ Ni²⁺(aq) and a silver electrode in 1.00 mol dm⁻³ Ag⁺(aq), at 298 K. The half-cells are joined by a salt bridge containing potassium nitrate.
E⦵(Ni²⁺/Ni) = −0.26 V   E⦵(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V   F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the anode and state the direction of electron flow in the external circuit.
markscheme: nickel is the anode / negative electrode
electrons flow from Ni to Ag through the wire

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write the equation for the overall cell reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the standard cell potential, E⦵cell.
parts.notes: Reject multiplying the Ag⁺/Ag potential by 2.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Calculate the standard Gibbs energy change, ΔG⦵, for the cell reaction in kJ.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Explain the role of the salt bridge and state the direction in which nitrate ions move through it.
markscheme: allows ions to move between half-cells to balance charge / completes the circuit without mixing the solutions
NO₃⁻ ions move towards the nickel half-cell (anode), where positive Ni²⁺ ions are being produced
